# Cycle 1 goal

## Client statement

> Honestly, the way I do it now is a mess. I paste links into a notes file and I can never find anything later, and half the time I've saved the same page twice without realizing.
>
> So when this is finished, here's what I'd want to feel different:
>
> When I save a link, I shouldn't have to type out what it is — I'd want the app to go grab the page's title and a little description and the site's icon automatically, so my list actually looks like something I can read and recognize at a glance, not just a wall of raw web addresses. And if I try to save something I've already saved, I don't want a second copy — I'd expect it to just take me to the one I already have so I can update it.
>
> Then I need to actually *find* things again. I'd want to search across everything I've saved, and I'd want to label things so I can pull up, say, just my recipes or just my work stuff.
>
> And I want to manage them over time — mark some as "I'll read this later" and see just those, edit or delete ones I don't want, and tidy up in bulk when my list gets long.
>
> That's the heart of it for me.

## Confirmed direction

Create a bookmark app that replaces the client's notes-file workflow with a readable, searchable, organized collection; automatically identifies saved pages; prevents duplicate entries; and supports later reading, editing, deleting, and bulk cleanup.

## Interface form

> A web app makes the most sense to me. I mostly run into links while I'm at my computer browsing, so I'd want to just open it in my browser and have everything there. It's really only for me — it's my own personal collection, not something I need other people logging into.
>
> If it happens to work okay on my phone screen too, that's a nice bonus, but I'm not picturing a separate phone app or anything I'd install. Web is the priority.
# Non-functional backlog

## Cycle 1

- Card controls should remain clear and leave room for additional saved-item actions as they are introduced; the visible Edit action must not become buried merely because more actions exist.
# Development

Phase 2. Design and implement based on the Gherkin specification.

---

## Context-dependent behaviour

| Context | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| First cycle | Full design and implementation |
| Later cycles | Reflect the design of affected parts and fix the implementation |

---

## Implementation basis

Use the GWT (Gherkin) of approved scenarios as the basis for functional behaviour.
Do not arbitrarily add behaviour not included in the Gherkin.
Do not reference, copy, adapt, or reuse Phase 1 prototype code as a basis for
Phase 2 implementation. Carry approved behaviour forward through the approved
scenarios' GWT specifications. Develop the production code in `implementation/`,
separately from the exploration code in `prototypes/`.

This restriction applies to exploration code, including prototypes made in later
cycles. Later cycles may modify the existing production implementation according
to the updated approved GWT; they do not require rebuilding it from scratch.

---

## Internal information system

Accumulate the following information during implementation. Keep the format
lightweight, but at a level that enables impact analysis in later cycles.

### Design-decision record
What was decided, why, and which alternatives were dropped.
Notes for understanding the structure after context is reset.

### Scenario-code mapping
Which scenario (SCN-NNN) corresponds to which code.
The basis for judging the impact scope on a change request.

### Tests
Create tests together with the implementation.
Include both Gherkin-based acceptance tests and internal unit/integration tests.

---

## Sufficiency criteria

The internal information system is sufficient when it meets both of:
- A level that enables impact analysis in later cycles
- A level from which, if the user requests traditional artifacts (design
  documents, test plans, etc.), they can be generated and provided

---

## Transition to Phase 3

When implementation and test creation are complete, switch to Phase 3
(verification).
